title: 現代建築論
subtitle: Contemporary Architectural Theory
educationalGoal: Starting with modernism that began in the 20th century, modern architecture has continued to change in various regions and countries. Behind this change are changes in global society and economy, people's lifestyles, values, and philosophies, as well as technological innovations in various fields. Learn how modern architecture has changed and evolved under these influences. In addition, through such learning, students will develop the ability to understand, design, and create architecture from a historical perspective and critical thinking.
advice:
Lectures will be given on the following topics related to modern architecture.

1. What is modernism?
2. Modernist architects and architecture
3. Modernism and Regionalism 1
4. Modernism and regionalism 2
5. Postmodernism 1
6. Postmodernism 2
7. high tech
8. Bubble economy and the end of the 20th century
9. Program and architecture1
10. Program and architecture 2
11. Contemporary Japanese Architecture 1
12. Contemporary Japanese Architecture 2
13. Exam
14. Architect Toyo Ito
15. Architectural Practice
requiredKnowledge: No special prior knowledge or skills are required as long as you have taken Architectural Principles in the 1st term and Architectural Design I and II in the 3rd and 4th term.

activityGoals.body: Able to understand the ideas and movements of modernism that formed the basis of modern architecture.
Able to understand the trends and ideas behind modern architecture after modernism.
Able to analyze architects' statements and designs and consider their value and meaning.
Able to logically explain the content considered in ③ above using diagrams, photographs, etc.

achievementLevels.ideal: Students will understand how modern architecture has changed over time, as well as the characteristics of architecture and architects that represent each era and ism, and learn about the books and examples introduced in class. Through research, students can deepen analysis from own perspective. Students will be able to understand the trends in contemporary architecture and the ideas and issues behind them, deepen their thinking about the background and factors behind the creation of new architecture and architectural culture. Additionally, students can develop their own work production while relating the above learnings.

Class outline explanation
What is modernism?
Learn the concept and outline of modernism,
which was created in the early 20th century
and forms the basis of modern architecture.

lessons.content:
Modernist architects and architecture
Learn about the ideas and spaces of modernism
through architects who represent modernism and
their architectural works.
Main architects: Le Corbusier, Mies van der
Rohe, Frank Lloyd Wright.

lessons.content:
Modernism and regionalism 1
Learn critical perspectives on modernism based
on ``Architecture Without Architects,'' held at
the Museum of Modern Art in New York in 1964,
and the various design surveys that originated
from it.

Modernism and regionalism 2
Learn how modernism changed in various
countries and regions, and the idea of

along with various architectural works.

Postmodernism 1
Learn the concept and outline of postmodernism
through the theories of Robert Venturi,
Charles Jencks, Aldo Rossi, and others.

Postmodernism 2
Focusing on the 1970s and 1980s, we will study

High Tech
Learn about the trends in the development of
construction techniques as architectural
expression, focusing on the architectural works
of Richard Rodgers and Norman Foster.

Bubble economy and the end of the 20th century

Architecture and Philosophy
Learn about the outlines of philosophical ideas
often referenced in the field of architecture,
such as structuralism, cultural anthropology,
phenomenology, and deconstructivism, and their
influence on architecture.

Program and architecture 1
Learn about the new values of architecture and

and architecture that occurred from the 1990s
to the early 2000s.

lessons.content:
Architectural practice
In the modern era, how should we consider
architecture and architectural culture when
designing architecture? Through teachers' own
projects and their processes, students will
concretely learn how to think about and design
architecture.
